newsitem.title: GREECE: BASKETBALL-OLYMPIAKOS THRASH PANATHINAIKOS IN GREEK CLASH.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-OLYMPIAKOS THRASH PANATHINAIKOS IN GREEK CLASH.

text.p: Greek champions Olympiakos made the first step to Rome's Final Four on Thursday, humiliating holders and bitter rivals Panathinaikos with a 69-49 triumph.

Olympiakos, European finalists in 1994 and 1995, earned the precious away victory with an impressive performance in the second half forcing Panthinaikos to virtually throw in the towel three minutes before the end.
Olympiakos now need one more win at their home court next Tuesday to advance to the last four. If Panathinaikos win, they will meet again for a third-leg decider two days later.

The match resembled the usual action-packed domestic clashes only in the first half (30-29 for Olympiakos) when the two clubs were locked in a point-to-point thriller with lots of passion, rock hard defences and tough fouling.

But Olympiakos were clearly the better of the two sides in the second half, dominating the boards with forwards Dragan Tarlac (16 points, 13 rebounds) and Panayotis Fasoulas (eight points, nine rebounds) and scoring at will from outside the D, mainly with American playmaker David Rivers (17 points)

Olympiakos' Serb coach Dusan Ivkovic used his second playmaker, Milan Tomic and guard Thymios Bakatsias to confine Panathinaikos' top marksman Byron Dinkins (12 points) and with no scoring power from outside the D the hosts had no chance.
They trailed 54-45 three minutes before the end and then literally gave up, producing several nervous shots and making no effort to pull down any rebounds.
Panathinaikos shot only 33 percent to Olympiakos's 51 percent. Small forward Frangiskos Alvertis added 12 points for the hosts but all the other Panathinaikos players were in single digits.
It was Olympiakos's first victory at Panathinaikos in two years, after five straight defeats. Some 18,000 disappointed home fans left the Olympic Stadium early, some of them in tears.
No tickets were given to Olympiakos fans to avert clashes and there will be no Panathinaikos supporters in the second leg at Olympiakos's 17,000-seat Peace and Friendship Stadium.
"We won the first match and we are one step closer to Rome," Ivkovic said. "We now have the home advantage but we have to match tonight's performance to win."

Panathinaikos, the most expensive club in Europe, had the best record in this season's expanded EuroLeague with 13 wins in 16 games while Olympiakos (9 wins, 7 defeats) suffered several surprising reverses.
Olympiakos recovered in recent weeks showing their strength with away wins against Russia's CSKA, and Yugoslavia's Partizan Belgrade to reach the quarter-finals.
Panathinaikos played without their main pivot, Briton John Amaechi, who is at odds with Serb coach Bozidar Maljkovic and was not included in the team.
Olympiakos beat Panathinaikos twice in the 1994 and 1995 European clubs' championship semifinals but Panathinaikos managed to clinch their first title last season, against Barcelona.
